Investor education

Mortgage Investing Guides for Canadian Investors

Mortgage investing means lending money against Canadian real estate in return for interest — directly, or through a pooled vehicle such as a mortgage investment corporation. These guides explain how it works, where the return comes from, what can go wrong, and the rules that apply in each province, in plain language and with the risks stated as clearly as the benefits.

Investor notice. This website is for general information and education only and does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy securities. Securities of Lendmax Capital Mortgage Investment Corporation are offered only under prospectus exemptions in National Instrument 45-106, by offering memorandum, to qualified investors through a registered exempt market dealer.

No securities regulatory authority has assessed the merits of these securities or reviewed this website. A mortgage investment involves risk, including illiquidity and the loss of some or all of the money invested. Distributions are not guaranteed and may be reduced or suspended. Target returns are targets only. Past performance does not indicate future results. MIC shares are not deposits and are not insured by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation or any other deposit insurer. Read the offering memorandum, including its risk factors, and consult your own legal, tax and financial advisers before investing.
